parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit is a single file, src/application/validation/inputGuards.ts, and it covers one concern: structural checks on untrusted input before it becomes a command. That matches its own doc comment. Each of the four exported guards (requireRecord, requireString, requireInteger, requireArray) checks one shape and fails through the shared ValidationError abstraction, so failures are reported the same way every time. No rule is defined twice inside the unit. For example, the trim-and-non-empty rule appears only in requireString, and the safe-integer rule appears only in requireInteger. The file doesn't go around any module abstraction, since every error goes through ValidationError. Both incoming parsers (product and order) depend on these guards, which keeps the structural rules in one place for both. That supports the module's cohesion rather than splitting it.
